A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a DNA mutation in a family with neurofibromatotic type 2, which is a genetic disorder that causes tumors in the nervous system.

we have defined a mutation in the NF2 locus that segregates with disease in this family and have demonstrated that the mutation is a missense mutation that changes a conserved amino acid residue in merlin.
the NF2 gene is the only gene known to date to be associated with the development of multiple benign tumors of Schwann cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of a DNA mutation in the NF2 merlin gene can be used to develop a predictive test for neurofibromatotic 2.
the NF2 gene is mutated in all families, and in all cases the gene is mutated in the same region of the gene.
the NF2 gene was the only candidate gene that was known to be mutated in NF2 patients at the time of this study.
